reuse.why: The new action reuses shouldFillCategory, averageToBudgetAmount, and the existing mutation infrastructure, although SQL still independently applies hidden-category rules.

duplication.why: Category queries and hidden-policy dispatch are repeated across actions, with four queries also duplicating visibility decisions made by shouldFillCategory.

placement.why: Eligibility rules remain in fill-rules.ts, database and spreadsheet orchestration remain in actions.ts, and handler registration follows app.ts conventions.

scope.why: All edits directly support the requested exclusions, new action, optional hidden-category inclusion, tests, or release documentation.

maintainability.why: Centralized template and fixed-group exclusions help maintenance, but repeated queries and visibility decisions require coordinated edits across multiple actions.

bypasses_abstraction.where: actions.ts: set3MonthAvg, set6MonthAvg, set12MonthAvg, and setLastMonthSpending filter hidden categories in SQL before calling shouldFillCategory.

disguised_duplication.where: actions.ts: conditional SQL predicates on c.hidden and g.hidden express the same visibility decision as fill-rules.ts shouldFillCategory in a different form.

abstraction_drift.where: shouldFillCategory gains template and fixed-group exclusion branches without new configuration parameters, while four action queries independently retain and extend its hidden-category decision.
